reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: I reviewed the MedicinalProduct resource context, the full StructureDefinition finding material, targeted R4/R6 StructureDefinition evidence for the root and key elements, direct behavior findings whose `affectedResources` include `MedicinalProduct`, and the shared Resource/DomainResource behavior list as context only. I formed the resource-level conclusion before comparing against the deterministic aggregate.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `MedicinalProduct` was trial-use/FMM 0, so the compatibility burden is weaker than for mature or normative resources. That materially softens path-level break concerns, but it does not erase the regulatory, supply-chain, and pharmacovigilance risk of losing or mis-mapping medicinal product definitions.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R4 MedicinalProduct is replaced by MedicinalProductDefinition and related definition/authorization resources, so a migration program is unavoidable, but low-cost preservation for identity, route, and local rename churn still deserves standards attention.

reasoning.thesisMd: The actual R4-to-R6 shape is not a mostly stable resource with isolated element edits. R6 has no same-named `MedicinalProduct` StructureDefinition; the high-confidence successor is `MedicinalProductDefinition`. Old instances, resource-type discriminators, profile canonicals, references, generated classes, REST routes, searches, and the resource-scoped `$everything` operation all need retargeting before the element-level work even starts.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration starts with a root rename from `MedicinalProduct` to `MedicinalProductDefinition`, then splits or redirects important regulatory product data across the R6 product-definition graph. `pharmaceuticalProduct` moves toward administrable/manufactured/ingredient/device definitions; package detail moves to `PackagedProductDefinition` while the same-named product element becomes a package-type code; manufacturing operation data is reshaped and authorization details move toward `RegulatedAuthorization`; and `specialDesignation` becomes separate authorization/use data. Some remaining work is mechanical path or type conversion, but the resource as a whole requires graph-level migration and mapping policy.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The resource identity break means preventing one extra local element break cannot make R4 instances validate as R6 by itself. That lowers the leverage of preserving every old field mechanically. It does **not** mean there is no point avoiding avoidable churn: retaining the old resource identity or a transition alias, preserving cheap wire-path names, and documenting endpoint/search/operation replacements would still reduce generated-code, route, search, and validation disruption for implementers who must already run a migration.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest standards-review candidates are the root identity rename and the local path renames. Keeping the `MedicinalProduct` resource identity while clarifying its product-definition role, or at least providing a formal transition alias, would preserve the largest amount of compatibility. Keeping `productClassification`, `paediatricUseIndicator`, `name.namePart`, and `name.countryLanguage` would have avoided hard wire-name breaks at low model cost. In contrast, retaining old `pharmaceuticalProduct`, package-reference, manufacturing-operation, or special-designation shapes in base R6 would duplicate the newer resource graph and create consistency problems; those are better treated as migration-map obligations once the broader redesign is accepted.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior findings reinforce the same conclusion rather than creating an independent migration shape. `MedicinalProduct-everything` is replaced by `MedicinalProductDefinition-everything`; removed-resource search surfaces and base CapabilityStatement endpoint inventory changes mean generic clients will not find the old `/MedicinalProduct` search/REST surface; and operation-advertisement changes affect discovery. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings may affect servers that also handle MedicinalProduct instances, but they are context only for this resource review.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate correctly identified `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = Yes` and `removed-or-replaced-resource`. I differ from its `migration-program-dominates` posture in emphasis: the migration program does dominate planning, but the resource still has standards-review-worthy low-cost preservation opportunities, especially the avoidable local renames and possible transition aliases for identity and behavior surfaces.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The high-level conclusion is high confidence because the same-name R6 StructureDefinition is absent and the successor/root changes are directly visible in local packages. Exact mappings for split data remain medium-confidence because no official R4-to-R6 ConceptMap or medicinal-product migration guide was available locally, and related R6 resources were not fully re-diffed in this resource-level pass.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 MedicinalProduct has no same-named R6 resource; successor is MedicinalProductDefinition
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the primary resource-level break. A conformant R4 instance has a different resource type and canonical identity from the R6 successor, so validators, generated models, REST routes, references, and profiles all need migration. Despite FMM 0, this remains standards-review-worthy because retaining the old resource identity or defining a transition alias would preserve substantial compatibility.

findingConsiderations.title: pharmaceuticalProduct reference was removed and split across other product-definition resources
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is graph-level migration, not a local rename. Old references to `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` have to be interpreted into administrable, manufactured, ingredient, or device definitions, often requiring target-resource inspection. It supports the conclusion that a migration program is unavoidable, although preserving the old field in base R6 would duplicate the new graph.

findingConsiderations.title: packagedMedicinalProduct changed from package resource references to a package-type CodeableConcept
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The same path name changed from package-resource references to package-type codes while detailed package resources move to `PackagedProductDefinition.packageFor`. This is a high-risk generated-API and JSON-shape trap and a supply-chain/regulatory migration issue, but it is largely a local migration chore once the R6 package graph is accepted.

findingConsiderations.title: manufacturingBusinessOperation was replaced by operation with changed children and authorization handling
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The old backbone becomes `operation` with changed child types and authorization/regulator data moving toward `RegulatedAuthorization`. This is compliance-relevant and requires mapping policy, but the R6 goal of separating process from authorization is coherent enough that it is not the best low-cost compatibility-preservation candidate.

findingConsiderations.title: specialDesignation backbone was removed from the product resource
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Special designations can affect regulatory incentives and clinical/regulatory interpretation, so they must be explicitly migrated and not dropped. The likely R6 destination in `RegulatedAuthorization` makes the break understandable, but the mapping may be lossy for species or indication details and deserves explicit guidance.

findingConsiderations.title: Several local elements were renamed, including productClassification, paediatricUseIndicator, and name substructures
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: These renames are the clearest low-cost-to-preserve breaks. The underlying concepts largely survive, and keeping the R4 wire names would not create duplicate data locations. This should not be dismissed just because the resource also needs a broader migration.

findingConsiderations.title: contact changed from direct Reference to a backbone with mandatory contact reference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real old-valid/new-invalid JSON-shape break, but the migration is usually deterministic by wrapping each old reference in `contact.contact`. It is a migration chore and test case rather than a resource-level driver.

findingConsiderations.title: crossReference changed from Identifier to a typed backbone with mandatory CodeableReference product
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This path may require semantic judgment about whether an old identifier denotes a concrete product reference, a coded product concept, or a business relationship. It matters for safety and traceability, but it does not change the resource-level conclusion beyond reinforcing the need for model-aware mapping.

findingConsiderations.title: Several coded/local value elements changed representation shape
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `Coding` to `CodeableConcept` conversions are usually lossless wrappers, and string-to-CodeableConcept for special measures is manageable with text. These should be covered in migration tooling, but they are not strong standards-review drivers under FMM 0.

findingConsiderations.title: Name usage language now has a required all-languages binding
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is only a potential hard break because legacy data using BCP 47 language tags should migrate cleanly, but nonstandard local language codes may fail required binding validation. It warrants terminology-expansion and sample-data checking rather than driving the resource-level migration conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional product lifecycle status as a modifier plus other R6-only content
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This does not make R4 instances invalid in the R4-to-R6 direction, so it is not a migration-unavoidability driver. It is still safety/business relevant for R6-to-R4 downgrade or mixed-version consumers because modifier `status` must not be silently ignored.

findingConsiderations.title: MedicinalProduct $everything is replaced by MedicinalProductDefinition $everything
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The operation replacement is concrete route/codegen/conformance work for systems that implemented the R4 operation. It follows the resource identity replacement, so it reinforces the same migration program; a deprecated operation alias would be useful but only partial while the old resource endpoint is gone.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For MedicinalProduct, this is the search-layer expression of the removed/replaced endpoint. Generic clients cannot simply carry old `/MedicinalProduct?...` searches forward; they need endpoint and query mapping to the R6 replacement surface.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises the old MedicinalProduct endpoint, which confirms that the break reaches deployed REST and conformance-discovery surfaces. It is derivative of resource replacement, but important for migration planning.

findingConsiderations.title: Base CapabilityStatement removed several R4 system-level operation advertisements
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This grouped behavior finding affects discovery of operations including product-related `$everything` surfaces. The resource-specific operation replacement should be handled directly; the grouped advertisement issue supports transition documentation and explicit server CapabilityStatement guidance.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This may affect systems that manage metadata for MedicinalProduct instances, but it is a shared Resource behavior issue rather than a MedicinalProduct-specific change. I did not score it as part of this resource's migration shape.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or require an authoritative R4 `MedicinalProduct` to R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition` migration map covering resource identity, canonical URLs, references, REST routes, search surfaces, and `$everything` operation replacement.

Standards-review the avoidable compatibility points: whether the `MedicinalProduct` identity can be retained or aliased for transition, and whether the low-cost local renames can be reverted, aliased, or documented with explicit compatibility transforms.

Define graph-level mappings and manual-review flags for `pharmaceuticalProduct`, packaged product details, manufacturing operations/authorizations, and special designations so regulatory or safety-relevant data is not silently dropped.

Validate representative legacy instances for language codes, cross references, contacts, coded-shape conversions, and R6 modifier `status` handling, especially for round-trip or mixed R4/R6 workflows.

Keep shared Resource/DomainResource behavior breaks in a separate infrastructure migration workstream; do not fold them into the MedicinalProduct-specific score except where local operations or endpoints explicitly reference this resource.

caveats: No official HL7 R4-to-R6 medicinal-product ConceptMap, StructureMap, or narrative migration guide was available in the local inputs.
The R6 input is a ballot build, so names and details may change before final publication.

Mappings to related R6 resources such as AdministrableProductDefinition, PackagedProductDefinition, RegulatedAuthorization, Ingredient, and ClinicalUseDefinition were considered only enough to judge the MedicinalProduct resource-level shape.
FMM 0/trial-use means this review should not assume broad deployed prevalence from break counts alone.
